name: Lau Kata Kati
region: Lower Bengal (also played as Kowwu Dunki)
boardDescription: Two triangular halves sharing a single central apex (butterfly board); each triangle is subdivided by two breadthwise lines, with one perpendicular line running through both triangles and the shared apex.
ruleNotes: Each side occupies all 9 points of its triangle; the shared central apex starts empty. Moves go to adjacent empty points along drawn lines. Captures are by the short leap and are compulsory, and continued captures from the landing point are compulsory. A player unable to move loses; if neither can capture further, the player holding more pieces wins (equal pieces = tie).
